head.title: Kentucky district lookup — districtry Kentucky
head.description: Tap the map or search a Kentucky address: county, Kentucky Senate, Kentucky House and U.S. House districts — and who represents you. Free, no login.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Kentucky, and who holds it.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Kentucky — every district that covers a point, and who represents it.
head.twitter_description: Click or search a Kentucky address to see every district that covers it.

source.answers: The Kentucky Senate district covering the point.

layers.label: Circuit Court
layers.rank_note: 57 circuits of whole counties, so smaller than a State Senate district and larger than a district court

source.answers: The judicial circuit covering the point. Kentucky's trial court of general jurisdiction.

boundary.label: Dissolved from the shipped county fabric by ky/scripts/build_ky_court_districts.py, following the county lists in KRS 23A.020.

source.people: The circuit and family-court judges of each circuit, from the Court of Justice's own county pages, which print the judicial circuit each was elected from. Family Court is a division of Circuit Court under Ky. Const. 112(6) and its judges are elected from the circuit, so they appear here. Jefferson's 30th circuit is read from the Jefferson Circuit Court's and Jefferson Family Court's own websites, because its county page lists no judges and links those two sites instead.

layers.rank_note: 59 districts of whole counties, Kentucky's smallest court tiling

source.answers: The judicial district covering the point. Kentucky's limited-jurisdiction trial court.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 120 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; this instance's offline anchor layer, and smaller on average than a House district

source.answers: Which county contains the point, who sits on its governing body, who holds its elected county offices, and who sits on the board of its conservation district.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: Every county's governing body and elected officers, from the Kentucky Department for Local Government's county directory (kydlgweb.ky.gov/Counties/), one page per county; built by ky/scripts/build_ky_county_officials.py and refreshed weekly by update-ky-county-officials.yml. In 118 counties that is the fiscal court — the judge/executive and the magistrates or three commissioners; Jefferson and Fayette are merged governments, so their cards name the Louisville Metro Council and the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council from the same directory's city entries. The officers are the county attorney, clerk, sheriff, jailer, coroner and property valuation administrator. The directory does not say which district a magistrate holds; the district beside a name comes from the 2022 general election results, and the Magistrate or Council District layer says which district a point is in. The card also names the seven supervisors of the county's conservation district (two districts in Logan County), from the Division of Conservation's sheet for each district, read by ky/scripts/build_ky_conservation_boards.py: each supervisor's name and the year the term ends, which is all the sheets give; re-read quarterly and in January after the November election (ky/WATCH.md).

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 170 districts covering all but 39 km2 of Kentucky, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive — 601 km2 mean feature area, just under a county

source.answers: The unified (every-grade) school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 170 features for Kentucky over 102,228.8 km2 of land, measured 2026-10-01

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER. Kentucky elects every county school board by division and every independent school board at large (KRS 160.210(1)), and this app has built neither roster, so the card names the district and links the Kentucky Department of Education. Recorded as the coverage gap ky-school-board-members.
source.applies: Kentucky — statewide, except the four areas the Census places in its elementary and secondary tilings.

layers.label: Census County Division
layers.rank_note: 493 census county divisions, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive — median 196.8 km2 of land (mean 207.4), measured 2026-10-15: smaller than a unified school district, larger than a city

source.answers: The census county division containing the point, and its county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 493 features for Kentucky, every one a census county division (LSADC 22, FUNCSTAT S), measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER. A census county division is an area the Census Bureau draws to report its counts: no one is elected from it, and Kentucky has no townships, so the county governs everyone outside a city. The card names the division and its county and says it governs nobody.

layers.label: Magistrate or Council District
layers.rank_note: 314 districts in 58 counties: the magisterial districts of 56 fiscal courts and the council districts of Louisville Metro and Lexington-Fayette, 169 km2 mean feature area over 53,163 km2, so smaller than a school district and larger than a city

source.answers: Which magisterial district (or, in Louisville and Lexington, which council district) contains the point, and who represents it on the fiscal court or council.

boundary.label: Kentucky State Board of Elections — voting precincts, composed into magisterial districts from the precincts on each magistrate race's ballot in the certified 2026 primary and 2022 general recap sheets (ky/scripts/build_ky_county_districts.py)
Kentucky State Board of Elections — 2026 primary recap sheets
LOJIC — Louisville Metro Council districts
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government — council districts

source.people: The magistrate or council member for the district, from the same county roster the County card reads (ky-county-officials.json, from the Kentucky Department for Local Government's directory). A magistrate's district comes from the 2022 general election results; a council member's from the government's own council map. A member the results could not match is not named on the district, and the card says so.
source.applies: 56 of the 104 counties whose magistrates are elected by district, plus Louisville Metro and Lexington-Fayette. The other 48 are not drawn yet because the published results did not place every one of their precincts; the 14 commissioner counties elect by the whole county and have no districts to draw.

layers.label: School Board Division
layers.rank_note: 13 features in 2 counties — the 5 divisions of the Jefferson County board, from the precinct lists in KRS 160.211, the 5 of the Rowan County board, from the 2022 and 2024 general election results, and 3 Jefferson precincts placed in no division — 136.22 km2 mean area (median 126.46), measured 2026-10-17 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a magistrate or council district (169 km2), larger than a voting precinct (32.75)

source.answers: The division of a Kentucky county board of education that contains the point, in the counties whose divisions this map draws (Jefferson and Rowan), and, in Jefferson County, the three precincts the statute leaves for the county board of elections to place.

boundary.label: KRS 160.211, created by 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 154, sec. 9 (effective April 14, 2026) — the precinct codes of the Jefferson County board's five divisions; the repository's copy (ky/data/source/statutes/krs160.211.txt) is held to section 9 of the act as enacted on every build
Kentucky State Board of Elections — voting precincts, joined to the statute's codes and to the election results by precinct code (ky/scripts/build_ky_school_board_divisions.py)
U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts): the Jefferson County and Rowan County school district boundaries each division is cut to
Kentucky State Board of Elections — 2024 general election recap sheets, which with the 2022 sheets place every Rowan County precinct in one division's race
Kentucky State Board of Elections — 2022 general election recap sheets

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER NAMED. No list of a county board's members by division has been read for this app, so the card names the division, says how it was drawn and links the board's own page. Recorded as the coverage gap ky-school-board-members.
source.applies: Jefferson County, inside the Jefferson County School District (the Anchorage Independent School District, whose board is elected at large, is in no division), and Rowan County. Elsewhere the card says the county's divisions are not drawn here yet.

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 3,194 precincts tiling the state, pre-built from the State Board of Elections' own layer — 32.75 km2 mean area, land and water (median 8.70), measured 2026-10-15 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a school board division (136.22 km2), larger than a city (12.00)

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point — where a reader votes and how their ballots are reported — and, up to Election Day, the polling place assigned to it or the voting centers its county opens to every voter.

boundary.label: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Voting Precinct Boundaries in Kentucky, compiled under KRS 117.055 to 117.0557 from the precinct files each county board of elections submits and hosted by the Kentucky Division of Geographic Information (CC0 1.0); 3,194 features, pre-built for the state by ky/scripts/build_ky_precincts.py and shipped with the app. The item says it is current through the November 3, 2026 general election and that a county's own records control where the two disagree, which the card says.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody — it is an election-administration unit, not a district with a representative — so the card says that rather than leaving a reader to wonder which name is absent. The polling place comes from the State Board of Elections' polling location workbook for the election (one row per building naming the precincts assigned to it, or ALL for a voting center any voter in the county may use), joined to the map's precincts by the state's precinct code, read daily until Election Day, with each building placed on the map by the U.S. Census Bureau's geocoder.

layers.label: City
layers.rank_note: 415 incorporated places, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive — 12.00 km2 mean feature area over 4,978.5 km2, under 5% of the state's land

source.answers: The city covering the point, if any. Kentucky has no township tier, so a point outside every city is governed by its county and the card is correctly empty.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / incorporated places, layer 4, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 415 features for Kentucky, measured 2026-10-01, every one carrying the Census's city descriptor — Kentucky incorporates no villages or towns, so this card needs no type row

source.people: The mayor and the city council or commission of each city, from the Kentucky Department for Local Government's municipal directory (kydlgweb.ky.gov/Cities/), read county by county and joined to the Census place id by name and checked against the county the directory names; built by ky/scripts/build_ky_city_officials.py and refreshed weekly by update-ky-city-officials.yml. Staff the directory lists beside them (clerk, attorney, chiefs) are left out. The directory dates nothing, so the card prints the day it was read.
source.applies: Kentucky — statewide, answering only inside an incorporated city.

negative_point.note: near West Union, Adams County, OHIO, about 15 km north of the Ohio River — outside Kentucky, and inside permalink_gate (maxLat 39.30) so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-13: TIGERweb's state and county layers name Ohio and Adams County STATE 39 (controls: the Louisville anchor returns Kentucky and Jefferson County STATE 21, and Columbus returns Ohio and Franklin County STATE 39, so the query answers rather than failing), and no outline in fleet-outlines.json contained it then, with Tennessee's outline in that file (control: the Louisville anchor IS inside Kentucky's outline there). OHIO'S OUTLINE HAS COVERED THIS POINT SINCE THE CHANGE THAT PUBLISHED OHIO (batch 2 of the state-level launch, written 2026-11-11), AND THE POINT STAYS: measured that day on a 0.02-degree grid, no ground in this app's gate lies more than 2 km from every outline in fleet-outlines.json, because Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, West Virginia, Virginia, Tennessee and Missouri are all served. It is still outside Kentucky and outside every shipped boundary file, which is all the checks that boot on it ask, and a selection the app makes itself never leaves. THIS POINT WAS IN SUMNER COUNTY, TENNESSEE UNTIL TENNESSEE'S GO-LIVE, chosen on 2026-09-30 because no instance covered Tennessee; that change put Tennessee's outline in the fleet file with the old point inside it, so a Kentucky selection there would have handed off to districtry.com/tn/. OHIO WAS CHOSEN on 2026-10-13 because Illinois, Indiana, Tennessee, Missouri and Virginia were live then and the states planned next did not border Kentucky; West Virginia, which went live on 2026-11-10, does not contain this point either. THE POINT IS ON LAND, NOT ON WATER: Kentucky's TIGER county fabric follows the Ohio River's north bank, so the river is INSIDE Kentucky rather than outside it, and a point in open water on the northern border would be inside a Kentucky county exactly as Minnesota's Lake Superior candidate was inside Cook County.

geometry.note: The whole-Kentucky-state outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from all 120 counties' TIGERweb State_County layer-1 geometry by ky/scripts/build_metro_outline.py (METRO_COUNTY_FIPS = every county; DISPATCH_COUNTY_FIPS empty — no layer is county-keyed yet). Kentucky is 2-band coverage: its county tier and its statewide tier coincide, so there is no second, wider region file and coverage_key declares no region.
Every county, pre-built from TIGERweb State_County layer 1.
U.S. House districts, pre-built from TIGERweb Legislative layer 0.
Kentucky Senate districts, pre-built by ky/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate, plus the shared-outline gate against the other two chambers).

Kentucky House districts, pre-built by ky/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py. They do NOT nest inside the Senate districts, so there is no nesting gate here; the cross-layer gate is the shared state outline.
The 7 Supreme Court districts of KRS 21A.010, dissolved from the county fabric. The Court of Appeals layer draws this same file: KRS 22A.010(2) gives it the Supreme Court's districts.
The 57 judicial circuits of KRS 23A.020, dissolved from the county fabric.
The 59 judicial districts of KRS 24A.030, dissolved from the county fabric. A second version is already enacted for 2031-01-01, taking it to 58; WATCH.md carries the row.

Magisterial and council districts, built by ky/scripts/build_ky_county_districts.py from the State Board of Elections' precinct map and recap sheets and from Louisville's and Lexington's council maps; its --check holds the file to its source record and each drawn county to its Census outline.

Every Kentucky voting precinct, pre-built by ky/scripts/build_ky_precincts.py through scripts/statewide_precincts.py from the State Board of Elections' layer (Douglas-Peucker at 8 m, the smallest of 4, 8 and 12 m that keeps the file at or under 2.5 MB gzipped; a 6,000-point agreement gate, measured 99.98% with zero overlaps; an exact 3,194 count on the fetch and the drawn file). 10.2 MB, 2.49 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

County school board divisions, built by ky/scripts/build_ky_school_board_divisions.py: Jefferson County's five from the precinct lists in KRS 160.211 and Rowan County's five from the 2022 and 2024 general election recap sheets, each cut to its Census school district, plus three Jefferson precincts the statute does not list, shipped whole and placed in no division. Its --check holds the file to its source record, the statute as kept in the repository and the precinct codes in ky-precincts.json.

rosters.note: The officers Kentucky elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from ky/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
U.S. House roster, refreshed weekly by update-ky-congress-roster.yml.
The Data gaps panel's content, emitted from docs/DATA_LAYER_GUIDEBOOK.md's gaps block: the fiscal courts, the two legislature rosters, and the county officers.

Kentucky's judges, keyed by the numbered district or circuit each was elected from, from the Court of Justice's own pages; refreshed weekly by update-ky-judges-roster.yml. Jefferson's circuit 30 and district 30 are recorded as asked about rather than left silent.
Each Kentucky city's mayor and council or commission, keyed by Census place id, from the Department for Local Government's municipal directory; refreshed weekly by update-ky-city-officials.yml.
Each Kentucky county's governing body and elected officers, keyed by county GEOID, from the Department for Local Government's county directory; refreshed weekly by update-ky-county-officials.yml.

Each precinct's Election Day polling place (sites[] plus precincts{map key: site index}) and each county's voting centers (centers{county FIPS: [site index]}) from the State Board of Elections' polling location workbook for the 2026-11-03 election, joined to ky-precincts.json by the state's precinct code, by ky/scripts/build_ky_polling_places.py, refreshed daily; the build fails on a code not on the map, a precinct sent to two buildings or a county missing, and places each building with the Census geocoder (unlisted names the precincts with neither a building nor a county center). The card hides the rows after electionDate. Network-first: a moved polling place must reach a returning visitor at once

The supervisors of each county's conservation district (two in Logan County), keyed by county GEOID, read from the Division of Conservation's sheet for each district by ky/scripts/build_ky_conservation_boards.py, whose --check holds the file to its record of the sheets read and to the County card's wording. Re-read quarterly and in January after the November election (ky/WATCH.md).
